ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The mandatory PEP and sanctions screening protocol requires the following before any entity is incorporated: (i) screening of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, senior managers, and authorized representatives against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list; (ii) politically exposed persons (PEP) screening against the World Bank Listing of Debarred Firms, national PEP databases, and domestic position-based lists covering officials of the Chinese Communist Party and their family members; (iii) adverse media and regulatory disciplinary history checks; (iv) verification of source of wealth and source of funds for all capital contributions to the WFOE; and (v) continuous refreshment of screenings at least every 30 days from the date of name reservation to license issuance and, after incorporation, annually for the first five years. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years after the closure of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) – National Enterprise Name Reservation and Registration Online Service Platform, integrated with the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (https://www.gsxt.gov.cn)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be registered in Simplified Chinese script following the four-tier statutory structure: (1) administrative division (e.g., Shanghai, Shenzhen or a free trade zone name), (2) distinctive trade name chosen by the applicant, (3) industry or business character (here the mandatory Chinese-language token denoting 'customs declaration' and 'customs brokerage', based on the ISIC 5229 scope), and (4) company form (the Chinese statutory suffix equivalent to 'Limited Liability Company' in its full or abbreviated statutory variant). The trade name of a foreign shareholder may be transliterated phonetically into Chinese characters, but the transliteration must not be misleading, contrary to public order, or conflict with a prior registered name. English names are not registered with SAMR; however, the WFOE may use a corresponding English name for customs, tax and banking purposes, and that English name must be declared in the registration at the local customs authority and tax authority without legal effect on the Chinese statutory name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant shall first obtain the written rejection notice from the SAMR online portal. Within 60 days following receipt, an administrative reconsideration application may be submitted to the local municipal Market Regulation Bureau or the People's Government at the same level, under the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the People's Republic of China; the application must state the legal grounds and attach the original rejection notice, the proposed name in Chinese, and any evidence of lawful pre-existing rights (e.g., trademark registration, prior Chinese entity name, or a consent letter from the conflicting name holder). Alternatively, the applicant may abandon the contested name, correct the prohibited token or conflict, and immediately resubmit a revised name reservation request. Where the rejection is not based on a legal rule but on administrative discretion, the applicant may additionally file an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months of the rejection. If the 30-day reservation period is about to expire while an appeal is pending, the applicant should file a written extension request not less than five working days before expiry, supported by the appeal receipt.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or shared 'registered-address-only' service is categorically rejected for a customs brokerage WFOE. The Company Law and SAMR registration measures require a fixed, independently leased non-residential office address with a lease term generally not less than one year; the General Administration of Customs (GACC) requires, for approval of a Customs Brokerage Registration Certificate, an operational physical site with customs broker personnel, record-keeping facilities, and a dedicated customs clearance operations area. The local tax authority further rejects virtual addresses because on-site inspection of accounting books and fiscal control device placement cannot be performed. Accordingly, the constituent document package for incorporation must include a filed commercial lease agreement and, for customs brokerage, a location plan and evidence of staff presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspections: (1) entity name plate displayed at the registered door; (2) full-time employees present at the address during working hours; (3) statutory documents (business license, customs brokerage license, tax registration certificate) available for review; (4) actual physical evidence of customs brokerage operations, such as import/export compliance records, clearance logs, and bonded receipts; (5) the lease agreement in original form and registered with the local housing administration; (6) utility bills (electricity, water, internet) issued in the name of the WFOE. Quantified risk: 80% to 90% probability of at least one unannounced joint inspection by the local SAMR and the tax authority during the first six months after

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 amendment), articles 5, 6, 26–42, 46–48, 51–61; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, together with the provincial/municipal Electronic Tax Bureau e-filing platform maintained within the official chinatax.gov.cn domain; for any Hong Kong SAR parent or branch presence, the statutory counterpart is the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of the Hong Kong SAR under the Business Registration Ordinance and the Inland Revenue Ordinance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The China WFOE must first register with the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) and obtain the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory tax identification number for enterprises in Mainland China. Within 30 days of obtaining the business licence, the WFOE must complete tax registration with the competent local STA office through the Electronic Tax Bureau platform, submitting the business licence, articles of association, registered-address evidence, ultimate beneficial ownership and investor identity materials, bank account details, and a description of the customs brokerage and bonded transit business scope. The tax registration yields the taxpayer classification, VAT filing profile, and mandatory access to the STA e-invoicing and tax control systems. The WFOE must also separately register with the General Administration of Customs (GACC) as a licensed customs broker; that customs registration is not a substitute for tax registration. If annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed CNY 5,000,000, the WFOE must register as a general VAT taxpayer; below that threshold it may remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer. A foreign non-resident entity, including a Hong Kong shareholder, with no permanent establishment in Mainland China is not required to obtain a PRC USCC solely for holding shares; however, if it derives China-source income subject to withholding, the PRC payer must file withholding registration and the non-resident will be assigned a non-resident tax registration number in connection with treaty relief, withholding settlement, or non-resident contract registration. If the Hong Kong entity establishes a permanent establishment in Mainland China, it must undergo full foreign-enterprise tax registration and obtain the corresponding tax identification code from the STA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. PRC law does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election. The WFOE is automatically treated as a Chinese resident enterprise taxed at entity level on worldwide income under the Corporate Income Tax Law. The only material election is the VAT status between small-scale taxpayer and general taxpayer, subject to accounting capability and the CNY 5,000,000 annual turnover threshold. Hong Kong’s territorial profits tax operates separately for the Hong Kong parent, but no Hong Kong election can change the PRC WFOE’s entity-level taxation classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) in Mainland China; the Hong Kong SAR has no general VAT/GST or sales-and-use tax, but imposes profits tax, business registration fees and certain duties.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 aggregate annual taxable turnover is the mandatory legal threshold for general VAT taxpayer registration in Mainland China; every entity making taxable supplies must complete VAT registration regardless of turnover, and small-scale taxpayers whose aggregate sales do not exceed CNY 5,000,000 may apply the simplified collection rate of 1% or 3% as applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices, including Special VAT Invoices and Ordinary VAT Invoices, must be issued through the STA-controlled VAT Invoice Management System (Golden Tax System) and the fully digitalised electronic invoice platform. Qualified taxpayers use all-electronic invoices requiring API-based real-time transmission, logic validation, encrypted fiscal stamping, and automatic upload to STA servers before issuance or delivery. Paper-invoice users must operate STA-approved tax-control devices with periodic clearance and electronic reconciliation. For customs brokerage services, the VAT invoice must accurately classify the service under the taxable services category and apply the 6% service rate, with any cross-border fee component supported by contracts and customs or transport documentation to avoid recharacterisation as domestic taxable services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports from Mainland China qualify for zero-rated VAT and the export tax rebate (refund of prior-stage input VAT) where the WFOE is the recorded exporter on the electronic customs export declaration, the goods physically depart China, the export sales proceeds are repatriated through official banking channels, and the export tax rebate declaration is filed through the STA Export Tax Rebate platform. For qualifying offshore digital or cross-border services, zero-rating is allowed only for services listed in the Cross-Border Taxable Services Zero-Rated and Exemption Catalogue where the recipient is an overseas entity, the service is performed and fully consumed outside Mainland China, no benefit is derived in China by a PRC person, and payment evidences receipt from outside China. Customs brokerage and bonded transit management services physically performed inside Mainland China are generally standard-rated VAT services at 6%; zero-rating is construed narrowly and may apply only where the WFOE proves the service is contractually supplied to and wholly consumed by an offshore service recipient, with no local warehouse, customs, or import/export clearance benefit arising to a PRC-domiciled party.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Goods Customs Declaration (electronic customs clearance record showing actual exit of the goods)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or international transport waybill evidencing physical export movement
SAFE cross-border receipts declaration and bank foreign-currency collection advice evidencing inward repatriation of export proceeds
Commercial export invoice and packing list issued by the WFOE
Executed cross-border sales or service contract identifying the overseas buyer and the exact scope of customs brokerage or transit services
Export Tax Rebate (zero-rating) application declaration submitted through the STA Export Tax Rebate platform
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA automatically cross-matches zero-rated declarations and export rebate claims with customs clearance records, transport waybills, e-invoice platform data, and SAFE foreign-exchange receipt data. If the exporter cannot evidence actual export, genuine offshore service consumption, or receipt of proceeds within the statutory 180-day repatriation window, the zero-rating or export rebate is retroactively clawed back, input VAT credits are denied, standard-rate VAT is reassessed on the original invoice value, and late-payment surcharge accrues from the original filing date. Under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection, penalties range from 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax for inaccurate or fraudulent declarations, and deliberate fraudulent export rebate activity constitutes criminal tax fraud under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, which also attracts blacklisting and loss of future export-tax-rebate eligibility. Any Hong Kong parent structure must satisfy commercial substance and beneficial ownership documentation requirements to prevent recharacterisation as circular invoicing, treaty shopping, or offshore tax arbitrage.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China's RMB is not freely convertible on the capital account, and a PRC WFOE must navigate both current account and capital account FX controls. Current account items are broadly convertible if the bank authenticates a genuine trade or service background; the WFOE can collect and settle export-related receipts and pay for freight, customs duties, broker commissions and software through licensed banks using the appropriate SAFE transaction purpose code. Capital account items, including direct investment inflow, shareholder loans and dividend remittance, remain restricted. Before the Hong Kong parent injects equity, the WFOE must complete foreign direct investment (FDI) information registration with SAFE or a SAFE-designated bank; a foreign exchange capital account is then opened in a licensed onshore bank. Conversion of foreign currency capital into RMB is permitted on a payment-purpose basis and any material change in the intended use requires an amendment to the registration or fresh documentary verification. Profit remittance to Hong Kong is permitted only after the annual statutory audit and Chinese corporate income tax final settlement; the bank must review the audited financial statements, statutory reserve allocation, shareholders' profit distribution resolution, tax clearance and evidence that registered capital was fully contributed. Export proceeds are not subject to mandatory conversion under the managed-float regime, but repatriation and verification rules remain strict. FX controls therefore create timing delays and documentary friction, so the treasury must pre-fund customs duties and tax obligations while avoiding any unverified capital account conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE total trade receipt and payment monitoring, export proceeds must be repatriated into a licensed domestic bank account within 180 days from the export declaration date unless a specific SAFE offshore retention approval is held; the WFOE may retain the foreign currency in the designated settlement account or convert it into RMB based on operational requirements. No statutory mandatory conversion percentage is imposed on ordinary merchandise export receipts in the current regime, but every receipt must be matched against the customs declaration within the bank's trade verification system, and expected proceeds retained abroad for more than 90 days must be reported to the bank for inclusion in SAFE's monitoring framework, failing which banks may classify the item as an exception and suspend future trade payments.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. An offshore digital EMI is legally barred from being the onshore WFOE's principal banking rail. Such entities are not licensed by PBOC as Chinese banking institutions, cannot open a CNY current account for the WFOE, cannot hold SAFE-monitored foreign exchange capital, and cannot provide the statutory payment verification needed for customs duties, tax, or cross-border profit remittance. Using a non-bank EMI for CN treasury would expose the company to compliance freeze and possible foreign exchange violation. The only permissible supplementary use is for the Hong Kong parent's own offshore multi-currency collections outside mainland, and even then the WFOE's SAFE-registered receipts and capital account transactions must pass through a licensed Chinese bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is mandatory for the WFOE's legal representative (or a locally resident senior officer holding an original notarised mandate) and at least one authorised signatory. Chinese bank onboarding requires original business license, unified social credit code certificate, statutory company seals, shareholder resolutions, and face-to-face identity verification by the branch compliance officer. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted for the first corporate account because PBOC KYC rules require actual identification before issuing bank instruments, and seal registration must be performed on the bank's own copies. After the initial in-branch interview, some tier-1 banks may accept subsequent video-recorded confirmation for facility changes, but the account opening and all SAFE foreign exchange account documents must be physically executed onshore.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Hong Kong parent is newly incorporated and cannot prove the source of funds behind the equity contribution into the China WFOE.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate of the HK parent, 24 months of corporate bank statements, audited financial accounts demonstrating net worth, notarised UBO register with passport copies, board resolutions approving the investment, a source-of-wealth declaration signed by the ultimate beneficial owner, and a professional reference letter from the parent's Hong Kong bank confirming transaction history and character.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customs brokerage business creates rapid small-value payments from multiple unrelated importers and third-country freight counterparties, suggesting possible trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customs broker license and customs registration certificate, client onboarding files with executed brokerage service agreements, underlying customs declaration records, bills of lading, air waybills, commercial invoices, insurance certificates, the company's transaction monitoring policy, and a sample reconciliation ledger matching Automated Broker Interface collections to duty payments for the past 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The legal representative is non-resident and the ultimate beneficial owner sits inside a Hong Kong trust or discretionary structure, complicating individual identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Government-issued passport and residential address proof, mainland work permit or residence permit if any, personal tax clearance from the country of tax residence, trust deed or settlement instrument with an independent legal opinion confirming beneficial ownership, PEP status self-certification, professional references from a licensed bank previously serving the individual, and an undertaking to comply with annual onshore tax filing and SAFE information duties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound foreign exchange capital will be converted quickly into RMB and paid to third-party bonded logistics providers at inception, raising concern over synchronisation with the declared customs brokerage scope.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed capital usage and cash-flow budget, executed bonded warehouse and transit management agreements, invoices from each third-party logistics provider, tax registration and duty-payment vouchers, Chinese tax invoices for planned expenses, payroll register in the bonded team, an independent audit engagement letter confirming that the ultimate third-party payees are contractually related to the declared customs brokerage operations, and a signed legal-owner declaration that no fund will be released without a corresponding commercial document.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE must complete FDI information registration in the SAFE/AMATS system before receiving any capital. The Hong Kong parent then wires the equity through its licensed Hong Kong bank via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's Capital Escrow Account at the selected mainland tier-1 bank using the SAFE-approved transaction purpose code for inbound direct investment and referencing the capital contribution under the sole shareholder capital schedule. The receiving bank verifies the sender, the purpose code, the SAFE registration and the beneficiary name, then credits the account under capital-monitoring restrictions. Conversion of the equity injection into RMB is executed under the settlement-by-payment system only upon submission of tax invoices or commercial contracts that evidence the intended use; a licensed certified public accountant may issue a capital verification report after the funds are received. Any proposed change of use must be re-filed or supported by the bank's compliance judgement before settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic customs charges, VAT and corporate income tax are paid through the tax treasury information processing system (TIPS) using the broker's Automated Broker Interface ACH sub-account in conjunction with the customs declarant licence. Cross-border trade disbursements are routed as follows: SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for freight, brokerage fees, overseas software and service payments under underlying contracts and the corresponding SAFE current account purpose code; Commercial Letters of Credit issued over SWIFT MT700/MT707 for high-value bonded goods imports where the WFOE acts as import agent; and Documentary Collections for lower-risk parcel transactions in which a full LC is not economic. RMB-denominated cross-border payments may be cleared through CIPS, while USD clearing uses SWIFT/CHIPS; each payment is matched to the corresponding customs declaration or service agreement and must survive the annual SAFE trade verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts for CNY/USD, CNY/HKD and CNY/EUR, supported by genuine trade receipts or payables and executed within the WFOE's bank-approved margin and credit line.

Onshore foreign exchange swaps and date-swap overlays used to smooth near-term CNY and HKD cash-flow peaks, provided the underlying exposure arises from actual customs brokerage fees or trade invoices.
Exchange rate options and range forwards available from tier-1 Chinese banks for current account and approved direct investment exposures.

Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards are permitted only at the Hong Kong parent level for protecting the group treasury value of future dividends; the mainland WFOE may not use an NDF as an onshore hedge because SAFE accepts only deliverable and real-demand derivatives for the licensed entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Hong Kong companies, regardless of size, must prepare financial statements that give a true and fair view; every limited company (except small entities exempted under Part 9 of the Companies Ordinance Cap. 622 with qualifying conditions) is required to have its financial statements audited by a certified public accountant (CPA) in Hong Kong. The exemption applies only to small private companies or groups meeting at least two of the following three thresholds in a financial year: annual revenue not exceeding HK$25 million, total assets not exceeding HK$25 million, and average number of employees not exceeding 50; however, the exemption is automatically lost if the company is a member of a corporate group that is not eligible, or if the shareholders holding 5% or more of the voting rights request an audit, or if the company is required to be audited under other law. For a licensed customs brokerage house (ISIC 5229) acting under the Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department license regime, the licensing authority typically requires a full statutory audit certificate as a fit-and-proper condition regardless of small company thresholds. Therefore the mandatory independent audit applies in practice for this WFOE entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) for companies with general purpose financial statements; HKFRS for SMEs is available to eligible small and medium-sized entities; ultimate consolidation under the People's Republic of China parent entity would additionally follow PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE) and, if the group publishes consolidated accounts outside Mainland China, IFRS as adopted by the group; the statutory audit must be conducted under Hong Kong Standards on Auditing (HKSAs) issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong has no centralized public UBO register; however the Companies Registry maintains a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622, Part 17A). Every company must keep a Register of Significant Controllers at its registered office or a prescribed location in Hong Kong. The register must record individuals with significant control (ownership >25% of shares or voting rights, or actual control) and relevant legal entities. The company must update the register within 7 days of any change, and provide it to law enforcement upon demand. There is no separate annual filing of the SCR to the Registry; instead the annual return (NAR1) requires confirmation of the registered office address and details of directors, members, and company secretary, and the company must ensure the SCR is continuously updated for changes in shareholding, including within 30 days for any transfer of shares. The Inland Revenue Department may also require beneficial ownership information under the tax transparency framework; a PRC WFOE holding company must reconcile UBO data in its PRC business registration annual report (Annual Report of Foreign-Invested Enterprise) filed via the 'National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System' by 30 June each year, disclosing ultimate investors and changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Debentures (Register of Mortgages)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 to USD 1,500 per year (Hong Kong registered office and company secretary services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 to USD 4,500 per year for a small WFOE group with customs brokerage scope, depending on transaction volume, intercompany flows, and group audit integration requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) rate for qualified High and New Technology Enterprises; Small and Low-Profit Enterprises with annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million may enjoy a 20% statutory rate applied to a 25% taxable income base, producing a 5% effective rate during the 2023-2027 preferential period; 100% additional super deduction for qualified R&D expenses; general loss carryforward is 5 years, extended to 10 years for High and New Technology Enterprises; no automatic patent-box or free-zone preferential rate for customs brokerage unless the WFOE is physically registered in a designated bonded zone or encouraged industry region with local preferential tax rate approvals.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Mainland China Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (A Class) - Form A100000, filed together with relevant schedules including Schedule A105000 (Tax Adjustment Items), Schedule A107012 (R&D Additional Deduction), Schedule A108000 (Foreign Tax Credit), and related-party transaction disclosures; filed electronically via the State Taxation Administration (STA) e-Taxation portal (e-tax / e-bureau system) and administratively supervised by the in-charge tax authority of the WFOE.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with quarterly provisional prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual EIT return is due within 5 months after the end of the fiscal year, e.g., on or before 31 May for a 31 December year-end; quarterly provisional EIT payments are due within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating income: gross revenue from customs brokerage, customs clearance services, bonded transit management, freight coordination, and ancillary logistics services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue derived from both PRC-resident and non-resident clients on a gross basis. If revenue is earned through a Hong Kong affiliate under a service contract, the arrangement must be supported by real service performance, proper invoicing, and an arm's length transfer pricing analysis; shifting Chinese-source service income to the Hong Kong affiliate without economic substance will be adjusted by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs: direct costs of providing customs brokerage services, including licensed broker salaries, third-party clearance fees, software licensing costs, and bonded warehouse handling charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs paid to Hong Kong related parties are deductible only if they are actually incurred, reasonably allocated, supported by valid contracts and payment evidence, and consistent with the arm's length principle. Invoices or receipts from non-resident affiliate service providers must reflect actual services; otherwise the expenditure must be added back in the tax adjustment schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges: urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, stamp duty, property tax, and other deductible business taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Corporate income tax itself, late payment surcharges, and administrative penalties are not deductible. Customs duties and import VAT are not treated as deductible EIT taxes; they are capitalized or treated under the applicable customs valuation rules. Stamp duty on cross-border contracts with Hong Kong parties must be reflected here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses: marketing, sales commissions, customer development expenses, advertising, and Beijing or overseas office sales coordination costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Service fees or commissions paid to a Hong Kong sales agent must pass the economic substance test; simply routing marketing through a shell company in Hong Kong with no employees or sales functions will trigger disallowance and potential transfer pricing adjustment. Document the actual services, fee basis, and business necessity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses: management staff salaries, rental, professional fees, licences, board costs, compliance expenses, and general office overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office or parent-company management fees paid to Hong Kong shareholders are deductible only if the services are actually rendered and are not duplicated by services already performed by the WFOE's own employees. The fee must satisfy the 'beneficiary and actual service' test and must not merely constitute a profit extraction mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses: interest expenses, bank charges, foreign exchange losses, and other financing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a Hong Kong related lender is subject to thin capitalization rules: the debt-to-equity ratio for non-financial enterprises is 2:1. Interest in excess of the statutory ratio or the arm's length interest rate is non-deductible. The WFOE must withhold enterprise income tax on outbound interest at the statutory 10% rate, reduced to 7% under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement if treaty relief is approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Asset impairment losses: losses from bad debts, inventory impairments, fixed asset impairments, and intangible asset impairments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduction requires evidence of actual loss and compliance with STA asset-loss filing rules. Receivables from Hong Kong related parties are carefully scrutinized; a write-off on an intercompany receivable without liquidation or proof of uncollectibility will be denied and treated as a dividend or capital contribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fair value change gains/losses and investment income: gains and losses from financial instruments, equity investments, and interest or dividend income from subsidiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from PRC-resident enterprises are generally tax-exempt, but dividends received from a Hong Kong or other foreign subsidiary may be taxable in China with a foreign tax credit considered. If the WFOE holds an overseas investment, complete the foreign tax credit schedule and substantiate the foreign taxes paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit: accounting pre-tax profit after operating income, costs, expenses, and impairment adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the book profit to the EIT taxable income by making book-tax adjustments for non-deductible related-party charges, excessive interest, non-compliant invoices, and transfer pricing adjustments. Any understated profit attributable to cross-border transactions with Hong Kong must be reported accurately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments: profit after adding non-deductible items, deducting tax-exempt income and additional deductions, applying loss carryforwards, and computing final taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ownership does not change the WFOE's resident enterprise tax computation; the WFOE is taxed as a PRC resident company on its worldwide income. Include the Schedule A105000 adjustments, loss carryforward tables, and transfer pricing adjustments; disclose any related-party transactions with the Hong Kong parent in the annual related-party transaction form.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual EIT return attracts a monetary penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 per month of delay under Article 62 of the Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL); late payment of EIT incurs a daily surcharge of 0.05% on the overdue tax amount. Under Article 63 of the TCAL, understating taxable income or falsely declaring expenses constitutes tax evasion, resulting in recovery of the underpaid tax, a surcharge, and an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount. Criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law applies where the amount of evaded tax exceeds RMB 100,000 and represents more than 10% of the tax payable, with imprisonment of up to three years for ordinary amounts and three to seven years for large amounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends distributed by the WFOE to a non-resident enterprise shareholder; reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement where the Hong Kong shareholder is the beneficial owner and has directly held at least 25% of the capital of the WFOE throughout the 12 months preceding the dividend distribution and the shares are not effectively connected with a permanent establishment in Mainland China.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the 5% treaty dividend rate, the Hong Kong parent must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department (IRD) covering the taxable year. The WFOE as the withholding agent must submit an application for the non-resident to enjoy treaty benefits using the STA's standard treaty claim form, together with the TRC, the audited ownership timeline, the Hong Kong parent's certificate of incorporation, board resolutions, and a beneficial ownership declaration evidencing real economic substance in Hong Kong (employees, office, decision-making, and bank accounts). The in-charge tax authority reviews the application before payment; if approved, the WFOE withholds at 5% rather than 10%. If the reduction is denied or if 10% has been over-withheld, the Hong Kong parent may apply for a refund within three years of payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate on gross royalties and interest paid by the WFOE to a non-resident enterprise is 10%. Under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement, the rate is capped at 7% for both interest and royalties if the Hong Kong recipient is the beneficial owner and satisfies treaty conditions, including the absence of a permanent establishment to which the income is effectively connected. Royalty payments must be supported by registered IP rights and actual licensed use; interest payments must respect thin capitalization and arm's length interest rates. The payer must withhold and remit the tax within seven days of each payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File) is mandatory in RMB terms where related-party transactions in the preceding fiscal year reach the following thresholds: RMB 40 million for related-party service transactions, RMB 100 million for intangible asset or financial asset transfers, and RMB 200 million for tangible asset purchases or sales. A Master File may also be required for the China-resident entity when the multinational group meets the STA's group-level threshold, currently RMB 10 billion of related-party revenue or a comparable consolidated group revenue size, as specified in STA Public Notice 2016 No. 42.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The WFOE is subject to Chinese EIT on its worldwide income, and economic substance is decisive for claiming treaty benefits and for rejecting any recharacterization by the tax authorities. Under the PRC General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) in EIT Law Article 47 and the beneficial ownership doctrine, the Hong Kong parent must demonstrate real functions, assets, and risks in Hong Kong; a pure mailbox company will be denied treaty relief. The Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) of the customs brokerage business, such as licensed broker decision-making, customs declaration preparation, risk assessment, and client contract negotiation, must actually be performed in Mainland China; failure to do so may shift profits or expose the structure to treaty abuse adjustment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion / False Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE intentionally understates customs brokerage revenues, issues or accepts false invoices, books customer payments into a Hong Kong affiliate account without recognizing the income in the PRC EIT return, or fabricates deductible costs through shell suppliers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law: recovery of the underpaid tax, daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%, and administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law permits fines and imprisonment of up to three years for tax evasion above RMB 100,000 and more than 10% of the tax payable, or three to seven years for very large evaded amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 23 of the PRC Company Law (2023 revision), courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally jointly liable for the WFOE's tax debts when the abuse of limited liability directly caused underpayment. The legal representative and actual controller may be placed on tax-related blacklists, subject to travel bans and exit restrictions, and face civil asset restitution; if criminal tax evasion is established, the responsible director can be sentenced to imprisonment and fined personally.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays excessive service fees to the Hong Kong parent without contemporaneous Local File documentation, charges non-arm's length interest on an intercompany loan exceeding the 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio, or fails to disclose related-party transactions in the annual related-party transaction schedule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 41 and 46 of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law empower the tax authority to adjust taxable income at arm's length and disallow excessive interest. Article 44 of the Tax Collection Administration Law imposes penalties for failure to provide contemporaneous documentation. The tax authority may assess interest at the benchmark loan rate plus five percentage points on the adjusted tax and impose an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false or missing transfer pricing documentation may be held jointly liable under the corporate veil piercing provision for the resulting tax deficiency. Their personal travel may be restricted through exit-ban enforcement, their assets may be subjected to civil restitution, and if the transfer pricing adjustment forms part of a broader tax evasion scheme, criminal liability under Article 201 of the Criminal Law may extend to the legal representative and actual controller.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent is a pure shell with no office, employees, or independent governance, used solely to receive dividend, interest, and royalty payments at the reduced Mainland-Hong Kong treaty rates, or the WFOE fails to monitor large suspicious cross-border client cash payments and thereby breaches the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law while also concealing taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 47 of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law (General Anti-Abuse Rule) permits the tax authority to recharacterize transactions and deny treaty benefits, resulting in additional tax, interest, and penalties. The PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law imposes fines of up to RMB 5 million for failing to report large or suspicious cross-border transactions, and the customs brokerage license may be revoked under the Customs Law for dishonest or unlicensed clearance activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the WFOE and the Hong Kong parent may face joint and several civil liability for the diverted assets and unpaid tax through corporate veil piercing; they may be blacklisted and banned from departing China or Hong Kong; criminal liability can include imprisonment under Articles 191 and 201 of the PRC Criminal Law for money laundering and tax evasion where directors knew of or authorized the shell structure and concealed income streams.
